note: Real-world corpus: five screen recordings made manually on a private machine, each paired with reference full-page stitches captured from the same pages by a DOM-instrumented tool. The recordings and the reference images are personal data and are NOT in git (see .gitignore) — this manifest is the committed description of the corpus: its geometry, the measured baseline, and the per-case expectations the benchmark enforces. Record your own equivalents to reproduce the suite.

cases.name: rw1_newsportal
cases.description: news portal, single page, deep scroll

expect.note: Single article. Measured 4735; the production JPG is 4737 (the manifest's 4744 and production's own reference are CAPTURED EXTENT, not document height — the scrollbar thumb puts this document at ~13000px and the user never scrolled that far). The page RELOADS itself mid-session; recognising the post-reload view as the same page is what keeps this at one page, so a drop to 2 pages is the regression this guards. The fixed video ad on this page is also the anchor for DYNAMIC_MIN_CHANGE_RATE: its pixels change in a median 23.6% of the non-scroll transitions they are observed in (p90 26.8%), against 1.6-3.9% for regions that only change when the user clicks (galleries, embedded screen flows). A drop to 2 pages here means the ad stopped being recognised as noise.

cases.name: rw2_textpage
cases.description: dense text page, short single-page session

expect.note: Reached the document bottom. Measured 3980 vs the production JPG's 3981 — 1px.

Page-for-page with production (6520/960/4320). Page 0 contains a -4563px scroll jump that is re-localized against its own canvas by CONTENT; if that regresses, the jump reappears as a bogus REVISIT navigation while the heights stay correct — so navigation semantics, not geometry, is what breaks first here.

cases.name: rw4_portal
cases.description: dark dashboard portal, 4 pages, very deep scroll

expect.note: THE re-localization case. The deep page is scrolled by DRAGGING the scrollbar thumb: 4356px in one frame step, so consecutive frames share no pixels and the identifier reports 0 matching blocks. Re-localized from the scrollbar to 11618 vs production's 11624; before re-localization this was 5542 plus a bogus third page. Production emits 4 stitches for 4 visits (2 of them the same deep page), so the page COUNT is not comparable to production — 2 is our distinct-page count. 4446px of this document was never on screen and is declared in gaps[].

cases.name: rw5_mobileframe
cases.description: mobile flow inside phone mockup, 19 pages (hard case)

expect.note: Mobile flow inside a phone mockup. Production emits 19 stitches under a HIGH sensitivity setting (a new document version per mutation); we merge revisits under Normal, so the count is deliberately not comparable. It used to be pinned at 5, which was wrong for a reason worth recording: 5 required the identity vote's concentration for visit [71..144] to land at 0.516, and sweeping the RNG seed at the then-current 120 samples showed its true value is 0.44 +/- 0.04 — the 5-page baseline was an artefact of seed 42, and every other seed gave 6 or 7. At 480 samples the value is 0.420 +/- 0.022, below REVISIT_MIN_CONCENTRATION (0.465) by about 2 sigma, so the visit is now reliably its own page and the count is 6 — with one further visit ([306..326], 0.552 +/- 0.037) about 2 sigma the other side of the same bar, which is why the expectation is a RANGE and not a number. Most of the frame is the phone mockup itself, identical between screens, so this session has no pixel-only answer to 'is a changed subframe the same document'; what it can still guard is that no document extent goes missing, which is what pageHeightsPresent asserts (the tall 1880 and 3824 stitches production also captured). Treat an over/under count outside [6,7] as hard.

cases.name: rw6_shopcatalog
cases.description: B2B power-tool shop, 9 pages, ajax product panels (crash regression case)

expect.note: Added 2026-07-31 because it is the recording that caught a CRASH the suite could not see: a subframe's rectangle is the median of its changes' x, y, w and h taken independently, so it could reach past the frame edge, and the recursion then sized a stitcher to it while the reader clipped what it read — masks of one size, frames of another, abort. Nothing in the 19 committed sessions reproduced it. A catalogue page with a cookie banner, a hero carousel, product grids and ajax quick-view panels; every page reports an in-place region, which is what made it a good find. Production emits 32 stitches under its own sensitivity setting, so the count is not comparable — 9 is our measured baseline and this is a drift guard. Stable across two RNG seeds (page heights jitter +/-2px between them, which the windows absorb).

cases.name: rw7_screenflow
cases.description: embedded phone prototype tapped through screen by screen (subframe + inner document case)

expect.note: Added 2026-07-31 as the real-data guard for the subframe machinery: a 361x507 phone mockup inside a 1678x1020 viewer, tapped through a bank-onboarding flow. The lab fixtures (gallery / gallery_video / gallery_scroll) cover the three branches synthetically; this covers them on a real recording, and its subframes[] expectation is what would catch a regression in the states or in the recursion. CAVEAT on the heights: the viewer page itself barely scrolls, so page 1's 1207px is one viewport plus ~187px that is probably still the mockup's own scrolling charged to the page — the residual the confinement test does not catch. It is recorded as a drift guard, not as truth. Production emits 34 stitches, one per inner screen, which is what our subframe states are for rather than our pages.
